mainTopic: Three answers (רבא, רב אשי, and רבה) to the clash between רבי שמעון's rulings on a מנחה brought for the wrong purpose
overview: This amud gives three answers to a clash between two ברייתות of רבי שמעון. One ברייתא says a מנחה brought for the wrong purpose still counts for its owner, and the other says it does not. רבא says intent for a different מנחה is fine, because 'וזאת תורת המנחה' makes all מנחות one law, but intent for a זבח is not. The גמרא then asks whether the same logic would make a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת valid, and brings different views on that. רב אשי answers that naming only a different pan does no harm, but naming a different kind of מנחה does. רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges him with a dry מנחה brought for the sake of a mixed one, and רב אשי defends his answer. The גמרא then explains why each אמורא rejected the other answers. It ends by starting רב הושעיא's question about a מנחה brought for the sake of a זבח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Which slaughtered offerings did רבי שמעון mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון meant by 'זבחים' when he said מנחות are not like זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does he mean by 'slaughtered offerings'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick clarifying question about רבי שמעון's words. It is setting up the short answer that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said that in זבחים the actions do not show which offering it is, so wrong intent ruins them. But some זבחים do have their own special procedure, so the גמרא asks how he could speak about all זבחים.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtered animal offerings

phrases.english: And what are 'slaughtered offerings'?
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי שמעון's earlier line that מנחות are not like זבחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies a word in רבי שמעון's statement from before this section
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'זבחים' mean every slaughtered offering, or only some of them?

steps.title: He meant most slaughtered offerings
steps.stepSummary: The answer: רבי שמעון meant most זבחים, not every one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Most slaughtered offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון was speaking about the usual case, most זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A few זבחים have a unique procedure that does show which offering they are. רבי שמעון's rule that wrong intent is not 'proven wrong' by the actions applies only to the majority of זבחים, which are all done the same way.

keyTerms.meaning: Most, the majority

phrases.english: Most slaughtered offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison is to most זבחים, not to every single one.

steps.title: רבא: it depends on what the wrong intent was
steps.stepSummary: רבא settles the clash between the two ברייתות by splitting the cases: a מנחה taken for another מנחה, versus a מנחה taken for a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult. Here, it is when one takes the handful of a meal offering for the sake of a meal offering. There, it is when one takes the handful of a meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the clash between the two ברייתות of רבי שמעון. He says each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of wrong intent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says a מנחה brought not for its own sake still counts for the owner. That is when the wrong intent was for a different מנחה. The other ברייתא says it does not count. That is when the intent was for a זבח, an animal offering.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
Taking the handful of flour from a מנחה, a key step of the service
For the sake of, with the intent of
Meal offering

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult:
Here, it is where one takes the handful of a meal offering for the sake of a meal offering,
there, it is where one takes the handful of a meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the contradiction between the two ברייתות, discussed before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא covers a different kind of wrong intent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to report opposite rulings of רבי שמעון about the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Intent for another מנחה: it counts for the owner. Intent for a זבח: it does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This splits wrong intent into two kinds, and the rest of this piece explains and defends that split.

steps.title: The פסוק behind רבא's split
steps.stepSummary: רבא grounds his split in the פסוק 'וזאת תורת המנחה': one law for all מנחות, but no such link between a מנחה and a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: A meal offering for the sake of a meal offering: 'And this is the law of the meal offering' means one law for all meal offerings. A meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering: 'And this is the law of the meal offering and slaughtered offering' is not written.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains where his split comes from. A פסוק makes all מנחות into one family, but nothing joins מנחות with זבחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all מנחות share 'one law,' bringing one מנחה with intent for another is still within that same law, so it counts. The תורה never wrote 'the law of the מנחה and the זבח,' so intent for a זבח falls outside that law and the offering does not count for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: One law: all מנחות are treated as one category
It is not written
A slaughtered animal offering

phrases.english: A meal offering for the sake of a meal offering:
'And this is the law of the meal offering,'
one law for all the meal offerings;
a meal offering for the sake of a slaughtered offering:
'And this is the law of the meal offering and slaughtered offering' is not written.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחָה לְשׁוּם מִנְחָה – וְזֹאת תּוֹרַת הַמִּנְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's split in step 3
steps.raayaObject: רבא's split between intent for another מנחה and intent for a זבח
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: all מנחות share 'one law,' so intent for another מנחה still counts. Intent for a זבח does not.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון gave a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבא: רבי שמעון himself said the reason is that the מנחה's actions prove what it is, not a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא says 'because its actions prove what it is'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא. רבי שמעון explained his ruling by logic, 'its actions prove what it is,' not by the פסוק רבא used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי שמעון's reason is that the actions show which offering it is, why would we need the פסוק 'one law for all מנחות'? רבא's reason seems different from the one רבי שמעון actually gave.

keyTerms.meaning: Its actions prove what it is: the way the מנחה is prepared shows which offering it really is
The teacher of the ברייתא, here רבי שמעון

phrases.english: But the tanna,
'because its actions prove what it is' is what he says?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין עָלֶיהָ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source רבא gave in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of the פסוק as רבי שמעון's reason
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון explicitly gave a different reason, the visible actions, so the פסוק seems unneeded and unlike his own words.

steps.title: The פסוק saves it even when the actions don't prove it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains: even where the wrong intent is not visible from the actions, which should make the offering invalid, the פסוק 'one law for all מנחות' keeps it valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he is saying: Even though it is a thought that is not recognizable, and it should be disqualified, 'And this is the law of the meal offering' means one law for all the meal offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רבי שמעון's words in a new way, so that his reason fits with רבא's פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a case of מנחה for another מנחה, the actions do not clearly clash with the intent, so you might think it should be invalid. רבי שמעון means that the פסוק still makes it count, because all מנחות share one law. So the 'actions prove' idea and the פסוק work together; they do not clash.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means: rereading someone's words
Intent or thought during the service
Not recognizable, not visible from the actions
And it should be disqualified

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַחְשָׁבָה דְּלָא מִינַּכְרָא הִיא,
phrases.english: Even though it is a thought that is not recognizable,
and so it should be disqualified,
'And this is the law of the meal offering':
one law for all the meal offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַחְשָׁבָה דְּלָא מִינַּכְרָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's reason, 'its actions prove what it is,' seemed to replace the need for any פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where the intent is not visible and the offering should be invalid, the פסוק 'one law for all מנחות' is what keeps it valid.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבא's approach, when a מנחה is brought for the sake of another מנחה, the פסוק 'וזאת תורת המנחה' keeps it valid even though the actions don't reveal the intent.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is throwing out רבי שמעון's reason. The גמרא is showing that the פסוק fills in exactly where the 'actions prove' logic alone would not work.

steps.title: What does 'but with זבחים it is not so' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how to understand the end of רבי שמעון's statement about זבחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי שמעון mean when he says: 'But with זבחים it is not so'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון meant by the words 'but with זבחים it is not so.' It is setting up its own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 said a מנחה stays valid because of the פסוק, even when its actions do not show its type. That raises a question: why would זבחים be different? רבי שמעון's original reason was about actions, and all animal offerings share the same actions (one kind of שחיטה), so that sameness should not explain why they are invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings that are slaughtered
It is not so; the rule is different

phrases.english: And what is meant by 'but with slaughtered offerings it is not so'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 6 explained the מנחה half of רבי שמעון's statement in light of the פסוק, the גמרא turns to the זבחים half.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the words 'but with זבחים it is not so' fit the new explanation, which is based on the פסוק.

steps.title: No 'one law' פסוק joins מנחה and זבח
steps.stepSummary: All animal offerings share one kind of שחיטה, but the תורה never wrote 'this is the law of the מנחה and the זבח,' so זבחים do not get the same protection.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is one kind of שחיטה for all animal offerings, the תורה did not write 'and this is the law of the מנחה and the זבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: although all זבחים are slaughtered the same way, the פסוק never includes זבחים in the 'one law' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might have thought that one shared שחיטה makes all זבחים alike, just as all מנחות are alike. But what saves a מנחה is the פסוק 'וזאת תורת המנחה,' and no such פסוק was written that joins זבח to מנחה. So זבחים do not get that protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
Even though
It is not written in the פסוק

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁחִיטָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן,
phrases.english: Even though there is one slaughter for all of them,
'And this is the law of the meal offering and a slaughtered offering' is not written.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 6:7 only says 'this is the law of the מנחה'; the words 'and a זבח' are not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁחִיטָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared שחיטה does not help זבחים, because the 'one law' פסוק covers only מנחות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This makes the פסוק, and not what the actions show, the real reason for רבי שמעון's whole statement, in both its מנחה half and its זבח half.

steps.title: Then a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת should be valid
steps.stepSummary: If 'וזאת תורת' makes all of one type into one law, then 'וזאת תורת החטאת' should make a חטאת slaughtered for a different kind of חטאת valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, a חטאת for חלב that was slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת for דם, for עבודה זרה, for a נזיר, or for a מצורע should be valid and count for its owner. After all, the תורה says 'and this is the law of the חטאת,' meaning one law for all חטאות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reasoning. The same kind of wording appears about the חטאת, so all חטאות should also be one law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from steps 4 and 8 is that 'וזאת תורת X' makes every offering of type X count as one law. The phrase 'וזאת תורת החטאת' exists too. So by the same logic, a חטאת brought for one sin and slaughtered for the sake of a different חטאת should still be valid and count for its owner. That would be a surprising result.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, then this would follow; it introduces an unwanted result
A חטאת brought for eating forbidden fat by mistake
It will be accepted, so the owner fulfills his obligation
A person who took a vow to abstain from wine and other things
A person who had צרעת and is now being purified

phrases.english: But if that is so,

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת חֵלֶב שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת דָּם,
phrases.english: a sin offering for forbidden fat that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering for blood,
phrases.notes: Both are brought for eating something forbidden by mistake: fat in the first case, blood in the second.

phrases.english: or for the sake of a sin offering for idol worship,
or for the sake of a nazirite's sin offering,
or for the sake of a leper's sin offering –
should be valid and effect acceptance,
since the Merciful One says: 'And this is the law of the sin offering',
one law for all sin offerings!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק-based rule from step 8 and applies it to the חטאת, to show where it seems to lead.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that 'וזאת תורת X' makes all offerings of type X one law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Unwanted result: the same wording appears about the חטאת, so a חטאת slaughtered for a different חטאת would have to be valid and count for its owner.

steps.title: For רבי שמעון, yes, it really is valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the result: according to רבי שמעון, such a חטאת is indeed valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי שמעון, that is indeed so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not push the challenge away. It agrees that רבי שמעון really does hold that a חטאת slaughtered for a different חטאת is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a 'yes, that's true' answer. The result in step 9 is not a problem for רבי שמעון, because his own rule leads there and he accepts it: all חטאות are one law, so changing one kind of חטאת into another does not make it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so; the גמרא accepts the point

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Shimon, it is indeed so,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by accepting its result.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The result that a חטאת slaughtered for another חטאת is valid seemed unacceptable.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון it really is valid, so his rule faces no problem.

steps.title: For the רבנן: valid for דם or עבודה זרה, invalid for נזיר or מצורע
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, a חטאת for חלב slaughtered for another plain חטאת is valid. Slaughtered for the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע, it is invalid, because those חטאות come together with a עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the רבנן, he said: a חטאת for חלב that was slaughtered for the sake of a חטאת for דם or for עבודה זרה is valid. If it was slaughtered for the sake of the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע, it is invalid, because those come together with עולות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds how the רבנן rule in this case. Some of these wrong intentions leave the חטאת valid, and others make it invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even for the רבנן, a חטאת slaughtered for another plain חטאת, one brought for a sin, is still valid. But the חטאות of a נזיר and a מצורע each come together with a עולה. That sets them apart from a plain חטאת, so slaughtering for their sake makes the offering invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי שמעון
Invalid
Burnt offerings, which are completely burned on the מזבח
Together with them

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, all חטאות are one law, so a mix-up between them does not make the offering invalid. For the רבנן, a mix-up between plain חטאות is fine, but slaughtering for the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע makes it invalid, since those come with a עולה.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the רבנן make every wrong-intent חטאת invalid. They agree it stays valid when the other חטאת is a plain one, like the one for דם or for עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: According to the Rabbis, he said:
phrases.notes: 'He' here is רבא, who taught this rule.

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת חֵלֶב שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לְשֵׁם חַטַּאת דָּם,
phrases.english: a sin offering for forbidden fat that one slaughtered for the sake of a sin offering for blood,
or for the sake of a sin offering for idol worship – is valid,
for the sake of a nazirite's or a leper's sin offering – it is invalid,
because these have burnt offerings together with them.
phrases.notes: A נזיר and a מצורע each bring a עולה along with their חטאת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving רבי שמעון's view in step 10, the גמרא gives the view of the רבנן on the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the רבנן: a חטאת for חלב slaughtered for the חטאת for דם or for עבודה זרה is valid; slaughtered for the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע, it is invalid, because those come with עולות.

steps.title: רב אחא's version: every such חטאת is invalid
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא teaches the ruling differently. In all the cases, a חטאת slaughtered for a different חטאת is invalid, because the פסוק says 'slaughter it for a חטאת,' meaning for that very חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, taught all these cases as invalid. The פסוק says 'and he shall slaughter it for a sin offering,' meaning for the sake of that same sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the ruling from step 11. In this version, every case of a חטאת slaughtered for another kind of חטאת is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11 the רבנן made a split. A חטאת slaughtered for another plain חטאת was valid, and only the חטאת of a נזיר or a מצורע was invalid. רב אחא removes that split completely. He learns from the word אוֹתָהּ ('it') that a חטאת must be slaughtered for its own specific purpose, so any other חטאת makes it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: teaches (a statement in a certain version)
invalid
'it', meaning this specific offering
for the sake of

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the word אוֹתָהּ can limit a חטאת to its exact purpose, even though 'וזאת תורת החטאת' seemed to join all חטאות together.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava,
teaches it as invalid in all the cases,
phrases.notes: 'All the cases' means even a חטאת slaughtered for another plain חטאת, not just the נזיר and מצורע cases from step 11.

phrases.english: "And he shall slaughter it for a sin offering"
meaning for the sake of that same sin offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ לְכוּלְּהוּ לִפְסוּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter version of the ruling in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any חטאת slaughtered for the sake of a different חטאת is invalid, because of the word אוֹתָהּ.

steps.title: רב אשי: naming a pan versus naming a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the clash between the two ברייתות of רבי שמעון. One speaks of a כהן who names only a different pan. The other speaks of a כהן who names a different kind of מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: There is no difficulty. Here, he took the handful from a pan meal offering 'for the sake of a deep pan.' There, he took the handful from a pan meal offering 'for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier contradiction about רבי שמעון. רב אשי gives a new way to settle it: the two ברייתות are talking about two different cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One ברייתא says the מנחה counts for the owner, and the other says it does not. רב אשי says the difference is in the words the כהן used. If he said only 'for a מרחשת' (the name of a pan), the מנחה counts. If he said 'for a מנחת מרחשת' (the name of an offering), it does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: there is no difficulty
takes the handful of flour out of the מנחה
a מנחה made in a flat pan
a deep pan (also the name of a מנחה made in it)
for the sake of, in the name of

steps.confusionAlert: The only difference between the two cases is one word, מִנְחַת. Without it, the כהן named a pan. With it, he named an offering.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: It is not difficult.
Here, it is where he takes the handful from a pan meal offering
for the sake of a deep pan;
there, it is where he takes the handful from a pan meal offering
for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חטאת discussion and returns to the earlier contradiction between the ברייתות of רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות that report opposite rulings from רבי שמעון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each ברייתא speaks about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות seemed to give opposite rulings for the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming only a different pan lets the מנחה count. Naming a different kind of מנחה stops it from counting.

steps.title: Why a thought about a pan does no harm
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains his split. A thought about a pan does not harm the offering. A thought about a different מנחה does harm it, because a wrong thought about a מנחה can make it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pan meal offering 'for the sake of a deep pan': he is thinking about a vessel, and a thought about a vessel does not make an offering invalid. A pan meal offering 'for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering': he is thinking about a מנחה, and a wrong thought does harm a מנחה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives the reason behind his answer. What matters is whether the כהן's wrong thought was about the pan or about the offering itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pan is not being offered, so a thought about it has nothing to harm. The מנחה is the offering, and a wrong thought about a מנחה does matter. That is why the second case does not count for the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: a vessel or utensil
has a thought or intention
intention, thought
makes invalid

steps.whatToRemember: A thought about the כלי does nothing. A thought about the מנחה itself does matter.

phrases.english: A pan meal offering for the sake of a deep pan:
he is thinking about the vessel,
and a thought about the vessel does not make it invalid.
A pan meal offering for the sake of a deep-pan meal offering:
about a meal offering, which a wrong thought does make invalid,
he is thinking.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנְחַת מַחֲבַת לְשׁוּם מַרְחֶשֶׁת – בְּמָנָא קָא מְחַשֵּׁב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב אשי's split in step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the reason for the split.
steps.terutzMaskana: A thought about the vessel does not harm the offering. A thought about the offering does.

steps.title: But רבי שמעון gave a different reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי. רבי שמעון himself explained that the מנחה is valid because 'its actions prove what it is,' not because the thought was only about a pan.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the תנא said his reason was 'because its actions prove what it is'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי. רבי שמעון's own stated reason does not seem to match רב אשי's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said the מנחה stays valid because the way it is made shows what it really is. That sounds like the reason is that the wrong thought is clearly false. It does not sound like the reason is that he spoke only about a vessel.

keyTerms.meaning: the teacher of the ברייתא (here, רבי שמעון)
its actions (the way it is made) prove what it is

phrases.english: But the תנא,
says "because its actions prove what it is"!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תַּנָּא ״מִפְּנֵי שֶׁמַּעֲשֶׂיהָ מוֹכִיחִין עָלֶיהָ״ קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אשי's answer using רבי שמעון's own words.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the מנחה counts because the thought was only about a vessel.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון gave a different reason (its actions prove what it is), so רב אשי's reason does not seem to be רבי שמעון's.

steps.title: What רבי שמעון's words really mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains רבי שמעון's words. Even though the כהן's wrong thought is plain to see, which would normally make the מנחה invalid, it still counts, because the thought was only about the pan. So רב אשי's explanation still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Even though the thought can be clearly noticed, and so it should be invalid, it still counts, because the thought was only about the pan.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading רבי שמעון's words in a new way. His words fit with רב אשי after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Its actions prove what it is' is not the reason the offering is valid. It describes the case: everyone can see the thought is false, and for רב אשי such a recognizable wrong thought should make it invalid. It stays valid anyway because the thought was only about the pan, and a thought about a vessel does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what he means
even though
noticeable, plain to see
it should become invalid

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, רבי שמעון's מנחה counts for the owner only when the כהן named the pan, not a different מנחה. רבי שמעון's words 'its actions prove what it is' fit with this.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַחְשָׁבָה מִינְּכַר הִיא,
phrases.english: even though the thought is clearly noticeable,
it should be invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: אַף עַל גַּב דְּמַחְשָׁבָה מִינְּכַר הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15 by explaining רבי שמעון's words.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Its actions prove what it is' seemed to be רבי שמעון's whole reason, which would not match רב אשי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The phrase means that even though a plainly visible wrong thought should make the מנחה invalid, it still counts, because the thought was only about the vessel. This fits רב אשי's explanation.

steps.title: What did רבי שמעון mean about animal offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון meant when he said 'but with animal offerings it is not so.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי שמעון mean when he says, 'But with animal offerings it is not so'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what one line of רבי שמעון's ברייתא means. It is setting up an explanation that fits רב אשי's approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי just explained that רבי שמעון cares about whether the thought is about the offering itself. Now the גמרא needs to show how רבי שמעון's contrast between מנחות and זבחים fits that idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings
It is not so

phrases.english: And what does 'but with animal offerings it is not so' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב אשי against the קשיא from רבי שמעון's words, the גמרא now explains the rest of that same statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of רבי שמעון's contrast with animal offerings, read the way רב אשי reads him.

steps.title: In a זבח the thought is about the slaughter itself
steps.stepSummary: Even though every זבח is slaughtered, its blood collected, and its blood thrown the same way, the כהן is thinking about the slaughter itself, and that kind of thought does make it invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is one way of slaughtering for all offerings, one way of throwing the blood for all of them, and one way of collecting the blood for all of them, he is still thinking about the slaughter, and a wrong thought about the slaughter does make an offering invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a wrong thought during a זבח is about the slaughter itself, and that kind of thought can make an offering invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since all זבחים look the same when they are offered, nobody can see that the כהן's thought is false. You might think that means the owner still gets credit. But the thought touches the act of slaughter itself, and that is exactly the kind of thought that harms an offering. This fits רב אשי, who said a thought about the offering itself is the kind that matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtering the animal
Throwing the blood on the מזבח
Collecting the blood in a vessel
The כהן's intention or thought during the עבודה
Makes it invalid

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁחִיטָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן
phrases.english: Even though there is one way of slaughtering for all of them
one way of throwing the blood for all of them
one way of collecting the blood for all of them
about the slaughter, where a wrong thought makes it invalid
he is thinking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל גַּב דִּשְׁחִיטָה אַחַת לְכוּלָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In זבחים the wrong thought is about the slaughter itself, which is a kind of thought that disqualifies. So even though the false thought cannot be seen, the owner does not get credit.

steps.title: Challenge from a dry מנחה offered as a mixed one
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא asks רב אשי why רבי שמעון said that a dry מנחה offered for the sake of a mixed מנחה still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, the son of רבא, said to רב אשי: About a dry מנחה offered for the sake of a mixed one, why did רבי שמעון say it counts?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges רב אשי with a case רבי שמעון ruled on: a dry מנחה offered with the thought of a מנחה mixed with oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said that a thought about a different kind of מנחה does harm the offering. A dry מנחה and a mixed מנחה are different kinds. So by רב אשי's rule this thought should harm it, but רבי שמעון said the owner gets credit.

keyTerms.meaning: A dry מנחה, with no oil mixed in
Mixed. Here it means a מנחה mixed with oil
Why?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rava, said to Rav Ashi:
A dry meal offering for the sake of a mixed one,
why did Rabbi Shimon say it counts?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב אשי's rule against another ruling of רבי שמעון.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's rule that a thought about a different kind of מנחה harms the offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dry and mixed are different kinds of מנחה, yet רבי שמעון rules that the owner gets credit. That goes against רב אשי's rule.

steps.title: He meant only 'for the sake of mixing'
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the כהן was only thinking of 'mixing' in general, not of a mixed מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It means he was thinking just of 'mixing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that in רבי שמעון's case, the כהן did not think of a different מנחה. He only thought of the idea of mixing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thought about 'mixing' in general is not a thought about a different offering. So it is like the thought about a pan, which does not harm the מנחה. רב אשי's rule stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Mixing, the act of mixing in oil
Just, merely, in general
For the sake of, with the thought of

phrases.english: He said to him:
It means just for the sake of mixing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the thought was about mixing in general, not about a different offering.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כהן was thinking of a different kind of מנחה, which should harm it.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was only thinking of mixing, which is not about an offering, so it does no harm.

steps.title: Then say the same about שלמים
steps.stepSummary: If a 'mixing' thought is read as general, then a thought of שלמים should also be read as general 'peace', and should not harm a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then 'for the sake of שלמים' should also mean just for the sake of peace in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב אשי's answer. If we can read 'mixing' as a general idea, we could read 'שלמים' as plain 'peace' too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a עולה slaughtered for the sake of שלמים does not count. But with רב אשי's approach, we could say the כהן only meant 'peace' in general, and then the thought should not harm it. So why does רבי שמעון treat it as harmful?

keyTerms.meaning: Peace offerings. The word also means 'peace' or 'wholeness'
If so

phrases.english: If so,
then 'for the sake of shelamim' too,
should mean just for the sake of peace in general?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 20 by using the same reasoning on זבחים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's answer that 'for the sake of mixing' is only a general thought.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one word can be read in a general way, the word שלמים could be too. Then a עולה slaughtered for שלמים should count, but רבי שמעון says it does not.

steps.title: A זבח is called שלמים, but a מנחה is never called just 'mixed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. The תורה calls the זבח itself 'שלמים', but it never calls a מנחה simply 'mixed', only 'mixed with oil'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, the offering itself is called שלמים, as it is written, 'Who offers the blood of the שלמים,' and 'Who throws the blood of the שלמים.' Here, is a מנחה itself called 'mixed'? It is written, 'And every מנחה mixed with oil.' It is called 'mixed with oil.' It is not called simply 'mixed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two cases are different. 'שלמים' is the תורה's name for the offering itself, but 'mixed' alone is not the תורה's name for a מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כהן says 'שלמים', he is using the real name of an offering, so his thought is about a different offering and it harms the זבח. When he says just 'mixed', he is not using the name of any מנחה, since the תורה always says 'mixed with oil'. So his thought is only about mixing, and רב אשי's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare these?
Itself
Is called
Plainly, without anything added
With oil

steps.whatToRemember: A thought counts as being about another offering only when the כהן uses the תורה's own name for that offering. 'שלמים' is such a name. Plain 'mixed' is not, because the תורה always says 'mixed with oil'.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'mixed' and 'mixed with oil' mean the same thing here. The whole answer depends on the fact that the תורה's name for that מנחה includes the words 'with oil'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defense keeps רב אשי's whole approach alive. Whether a thought harms an offering depends on whether it names the offering itself, as the תורה names it.

phrases.english: How can you compare them?
There, the offering itself is called shelamim,
as it is written: 'Who offers the blood of the shelamim,'
'Who throws the blood of the shelamim.'

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא מִנְחָה גּוּפַהּ מִי אִיקְּרַי בְּלוּלָה?
phrases.english: Here, is a meal offering itself called 'mixed'?
It is written: 'And every meal offering mixed with oil,'
so it is called 'mixed with oil,'
but it is not called simply 'mixed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 21 and so defends רב אשי's answer in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases from the wording of the פסוקים: what does the תורה actually call each offering?
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שלמים' and 'mixed' are both general words, so they should be treated the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שלמים' is the תורה's name for the זבח itself, so thinking it harms the offering. Plain 'mixed' is not a name the תורה uses for a מנחה, so thinking it does no harm.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבה's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבא and רב אשי do not accept רבה's answer. They hold the opposite: a wrong thought that is easy to recognize is exactly the kind the תורה makes invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: All of them do not say like רבה, because, on the contrary, a thought that is recognizable is what the Merciful One disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other אמוראים did not use רבה's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said a wrong thought that is obviously wrong (like thinking of a different מנחה) is simply ignored, so the owner still gets credit. The others turn this upside down. In their view the תורה's rule against wrong thoughts is aimed exactly at a clear, recognizable wrong thought.

keyTerms.meaning: A thought or intention of the כהן while doing the עבודה
That is recognizable, clearly noticeable as wrong
On the contrary, the opposite is true
The Merciful One (the תורה) made it invalid

phrases.english: All of them do not say like רבה,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means the other two who answered, רבא and רב אשי.

phrases.english: because, on the contrary, a recognizable thought is what the Merciful One disqualified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the back-and-forth on רב אשי's answer, the גמרא now steps back to review all three answers, starting with רבה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבה's whole answer to the contradiction
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: His reasoning is flipped: recognizable wrong intent is what disqualifies, not what is ignored.

steps.title: Why the others reject רבא's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב אשי do not accept רבא's answer. They do not learn from the פסוק "וזאת תורת המנחה" that all מנחות share one law.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not say like רבא, because "And this is the law" does not imply this to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other אמוראים did not use רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a מנחה for the sake of another מנחה still counts, because the פסוק "וזאת תורת המנחה" teaches that all מנחות have one law. The others simply do not read that lesson into the פסוק, so his answer has no source for them.

keyTerms.meaning: "And this is the law of the מנחה" (ויקרא 6:7), the פסוק רבא used
It does not imply this to them; they don't read the פסוק that way

phrases.english: They do not say like רבא,
because "And this is the law" does not imply this to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as the previous step, now applied to רבא's answer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק he relies on does not teach one law for all מנחות, according to the others.

steps.title: Why the others reject רב אשי's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רבא do not accept רב אשי's answer, because of the challenge רב אחא בריה דרבא raised against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not say like רב אשי, because of the challenge of רב אחא son of רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the other אמוראים did not use רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said a thought about a vessel doesn't matter, but a thought about a different offering does. רב אחא בריה דרבא challenged this from the case of a dry מנחה offered for the sake of a mixed מנחה (step 19). The others felt that challenge was strong enough to drop this answer.

keyTerms.meaning: A challenge or difficulty against a statement

steps.whatToRemember: Each of the three answers is rejected by the others for its own reason: רבה's logic is flipped, רבא's פסוק is not read that way, and רב אשי's answer faces רב אחא's challenge.

phrases.english: They do not say like רב אשי,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם קוּשְׁיָא דְּרַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא.
phrases.english: because of the challenge of רב אחא son of רבא.
phrases.notes: This is the question about a dry מנחה brought for the sake of a mixed one, back in step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the review of all three answers.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's answer to the contradiction
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It is weakened by רב אחא בריה דרבא's challenge about a dry מנחה for the sake of a mixed one.

steps.title: What was obvious to רבה and רבא was a question for רב הושעיא
steps.stepSummary: רבה found it obvious one way, and רבא found it obvious the other way, whether a recognizable wrong thought harms a מנחה. For רב הושעיא this was an open question.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter that is obvious to רבה one way, and to רבא the other way, is a question for רב הושעיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the issue רבה and רבא each felt sure about was actually unsure for רב הושעיא. It is setting up to quote his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבה, a clearly recognizable wrong thought is ignored. For רבא, a clearly recognizable wrong thought, like a מנחה for the sake of a זבח, does harm. רב הושעיא was not sure either way, so he asked.

keyTerms.meaning: Obvious, clear without needing proof
To this side, in one direction
It is a question for him; he is unsure

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַבָּה לְהַאי גִּיסָא,
phrases.english: The matter that is obvious to רבה in one direction,
and to רבא in the other direction,
is a question for רב הושעיא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא דִּפְשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ לְרַבָּה לְהַאי גִּיסָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the answers, the גמרא shows the central issue was not obvious to everyone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whether a recognizable wrong thought affects a מנחה: רבה and רבא each saw it as obvious, in opposite directions, while רב הושעיא was unsure.

steps.title: רב הושעיא begins his question: a מנחה for the sake of a זבח
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting רב הושעיא's question, which some say he asked רבי אסי, about a מנחה offered with the thought that it is a זבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב הושעיא asked, and some say רב הושעיא asked it of רבי אסי: a מנחה for the sake of a זבח...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting רב הושעיא's actual question. The case is a מנחה whose handful was removed with the thought that it is an animal offering. The question continues past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the clearest example of a recognizable wrong thought, since a flour offering is plainly not an animal. It is exactly where רבה and רבא would answer opposite ways. The גמרא also records two versions: either רב הושעיא asked it on his own, or he asked it of רבי אסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question
For the sake of, with the thought of
An animal offering

phrases.english: As רב הושעיא asked,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַבִּי אַסִּי:
phrases.english: and some say: רב הושעיא asked it of רבי אסי:
a מנחה for the sake of a זבח

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the actual question that the previous step said רב הושעיא was unsure about.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the law is when a כהן removes the handful of a מנחה with the thought that it is a זבח (the question continues beyond this point).
